tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target-like appearance) on older lower leaves. Leaves yellow and drop prematurely, exposing fruits to sunscald.
tomato_early_blight.possible_causes: High humidity, warm temperatures (24-29°C), splash dispersal from infected soil or plant debris, dense foliage hindering air circulation.
tomato_early_blight.organic_management: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves. Spray neem oil (5 ml/L) or copper-based organic fungicides (Bordeaux mixture 1%). Mulch around the base of plants to prevent soil splashing onto leaves.
tomato_early_blight.chemical_management: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L at first sign of symptoms, repeating every 10-14 days.
tomato_early_blight.prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation avoiding Solanaceae family (potato, eggplant, pepper). Use certified disease-free seeds and drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
tomato_early_blight.when_to_consult_expert: Consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or Agriculture Extension Officer if more than 30% of the plant canopy is infected or if stem cankers appear.

tomato_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous circular water-soaked spots with dark margins and gray or tan centers on foliage. Tiny dark fruiting bodies (pycnidia) visible inside centers.
tomato_leaf_spot.possible_causes: Extended periods of wet, warm weather (20-25°C), high humidity, overhead irrigation splashing fungal spores.
tomato_leaf_spot.organic_management: Prune bottom 12 inches of leaves to improve airflow. Apply copper hydroxide fungicide or bio-agent Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/L.
tomato_leaf_spot.chemical_management: Spray Mancozeb @ 2 g/L or Zineb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L. Always respect the 7-day pre-harvest interval before picking fruits.
tomato_leaf_spot.prevention: Stake plants upright, destroy infected crop residues after harvest, avoid working in tomato fields when foliage is wet.
tomato_leaf_spot.when_to_consult_expert: Consult an expert if rapid defoliation occurs despite regular copper or mancozeb applications.

potato_late_blight.symptoms: Pale green, water-soaked spots rapidly enlarging into large, dark brown to purplish-black lesions. White fungal growth observed on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
potato_late_blight.possible_causes: Cool, humid and rainy weather (temperatures 15-20°C and relative humidity >90%). Wind-borne sporangia can spread across miles.
potato_late_blight.organic_management: Apply preventative copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L. Cut and burn haulms 10 days before harvesting if foliage is infected to protect tubers.
potato_late_blight.chemical_management: Prophylactic spray of Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L. In case of active outbreak, apply Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1 g/L.
potato_late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers. Hill soil high around tuber roots to prevent spores washing down into the soil.
potato_late_blight.when_to_consult_expert: Notify district agricultural officer immediately, as Late Blight is an aggressive community-wide epidemic threat.

rice_blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with gray/whitish centers and dark reddish-brown borders on leaves; neck rot causes broken panicles and chaffy grains.
rice_blast.possible_causes: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer application, cloudy skies with light drizzles, high relative humidity (>90%) and night temperatures around 20°C.
rice_blast.organic_management: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L of water. Spray fermented cow urine and neem extract (10%). Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilizers.
rice_blast.chemical_management: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L at boot leaf to early heading stage.
rice_blast.prevention: Adopt balanced N:P:K fertilization (avoid excessive Urea). Use blast-resistant varieties like IR64, MTU1010, or Swarna.
rice_blast.when_to_consult_expert: Consult agricultural extension officer if neck blast symptoms appear before grain filling is complete.

cotton_leaf_curl.symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaf margins, thickening of leaf veins, and cup-shaped leaf-like enations on the undersides of leaves. Stunted growth.
cotton_leaf_curl.possible_causes: Heavy whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) infestation acting as viral vectors, warm humid conditions, nearby weed hosts.
cotton_leaf_curl.organic_management: Install yellow sticky traps @ 15-20 per acre. Spray neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 5 ml/L. Conserve natural predators like ladybird beetles and lacewings.
cotton_leaf_curl.chemical_management: Control whitefly vector using Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2 g/L or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/L or Flonicamid 50% WG @ 0.3 g/L.
cotton_leaf_curl.prevention: Cultivate CLCuD-resistant Bt cotton hybrids. Eradicate weed hosts like Kanghi (Abutilon indicum) and gutputi from field borders.
cotton_leaf_curl.when_to_consult_expert: Consult crop scientist if viral curl appears during early vegetative phase before flowering.

citrus_canker.symptoms: Raised, corky, crater-like lesions surrounded by an oily or water-soaked yellow halo on leaves, twigs, and fruits. Premature fruit drop.
citrus_canker.possible_causes: Wind-driven rain, leaf miner damage providing entry points for the bacterium, high temperatures (25-35°C).
citrus_canker.organic_management: Prune cankered twigs during dry weather and apply Bordeaux paste (1%) to cut ends. Spray neem cake extract.
citrus_canker.chemical_management: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L combined with Streptocycline @ 100 ppm (1 g in 10 L water) at 15-day intervals.
citrus_canker.prevention: Erect windbreaks around orchard borders. Control citrus leaf miner during new flush periods with neem oil.
citrus_canker.when_to_consult_expert: Consult horticulturist if canker spreads rapidly onto mature tree trunks or young graftings.

healthy_plant.symptoms: Leaves exhibit uniform vibrant green coloration, intact cellular structure, clean leaf margins, and absence of necrotic lesions, chlorosis, or fungal mycelium.
healthy_plant.possible_causes: Adequate nutrition, optimum soil moisture, effective pest monitoring, and favorable microclimatic conditions.
healthy_plant.organic_management: Maintain balanced organic soil nutrition with vermicompost and compost tea. Monitor soil moisture regularly.
healthy_plant.chemical_management: No chemical application required. Continue regular scouting and preventive care.
healthy_plant.prevention: Continue standard integrated pest management (IPM) and balanced irrigation practices.
healthy_plant.when_to_consult_expert: Regular seasonal soil and leaf tissue testing is recommended every 1-2 years.
